submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation is tracking the three source batches closely and shows no anomaly. Product assays (available up to 48h sample time, released at 52h): 0.008 g/L @12h, 0.0 @24h, 1.057 @36h, 2.866 @48h — matching the source batches (2.98–3.06 g/L at 48h) within normal batch-to-batch variability. DO2 online trace mirrors the source pattern (onset dip to ~7.0 mg/L around 27h, recovery to ~11 mg/L after 28h, ~9.6 mg/L at 52h), always well above the 2.0 mg/L oxygen constraint, with no indication of oxygen deficit (oxygen demand onset slightly earlier/deeper than source but recovered, and 0h below limit over the whole run). The source-calibrated forward model for KEEP predicts a feasible, healthy run: ~576 kg product mass, terminal ~6.9 g/L, minimum DO ~6.1 mg/L, no hours below limit, with all sensitivity members feasible. Interventions (feed reduction/air increase) would only perturb a normally progressing batch and risk reducing product mass; stop yields zero production. No intervention is warranted.
submission.uncertainty: Assay data are delayed (latest product assay reflects 48h, not 52h); the true current state could deviate. The receiving DO2 dip around 24-28h reached ~7.0 mg/L, slightly lower than source batches (~8.4-9.3), suggesting somewhat higher oxygen demand in the receiving vessel — still far from the 2.0 mg/L limit. The forward model is source-calibrated, not the hidden realization, and its parameter sensitivity gives min-DO range 3.5–7.1 mg/L and mass 576–583 kg; even the pessimistic member remains feasible. If future online DO2 showed a sustained decline toward constraint, an increase_air intervention would be the appropriate contingency; it is not indicated now.
